assumptions: The founder uses no Reckitt confidential information, systems, relationships or work product.
The initial target is EU mid-market organizations with meaningful packaging portfolios and inadequate existing specification-management tooling.
Specialist regulatory review can be contracted within the stated capital and part-time constraints.
Customer and supplier permissions required to store and process evidence are legally obtainable through ordinary contracts, but exclusivity and cross-customer benchmarking rights are not assumed.
Public competitor offers demonstrate category spending and alternatives, not demand for this candidate specifically.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Several paid audits from the defined beachhead, documented conversion into annual subscriptions near the proposed price range, representative fully loaded delivery and support margins, renewal or revision-driven repeat usage, measurable time or loss avoided, signed referral economics, supplier response and completeness rates, and executed rights allowing durable storage and appropriately aggregated benchmarks. A competitive win analysis against PPWR Connect, PPWRify, PPWR Check and incumbent PLM extensions should demonstrate a substantial outcome or workflow advantage.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: PPWR creates a genuine need to connect packaging specifications, supplier evidence, technical documentation and approval decisions. The audit-to-vault wedge is coherent, but the underlying workflow is already understood and served by specialist and specification-management vendors.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Regulatory duties, buyer-side supplier-document activity and public paid PPWR offers establish real pain and category-level spending. Willingness to pay this candidate's 10,000–25,000 PLN audit and 24,000–90,000 PLN subscription remains unvalidated, while phased obligations make urgency portfolio-dependent.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid audits can fund discovery and annual subscriptions could provide favorable cash conversion and recurring revenue. However, the proposed pricing, 75–85% contribution margin, CAC, audit conversion, onboarding burden, specialist review, churn and payback lack delivered-customer evidence, and low-priced substitutes put pressure on achievable software pricing.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: EU mid-market brands and manufacturers without adequate PLM form a plausible focused beachhead, and regulatory scope is meaningful. Its economically reachable size is unknown because there is no evidence quantifying buyers with both inadequate incumbent tooling and budgets for this higher-priced offer.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: The candidate could specialize around a lightweight implementation experience for underserved mid-market accounts, but direct tools already offer declarations, repositories and supplier workflows, while Specright bundles the core functions. No exclusive channel, mandate, dataset or rights position supports likely segment domination.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful packaging evidence record could expand across additional suppliers, SKUs, countries, evolving PPWR requirements and adjacent packaging-compliance workflows. Expansion is credible in concept, although it depends on obtaining reusable permissions and first proving a differentiated beachhead.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Workflow embedding, accumulated schemas and response benchmarks could compound, but customers and suppliers currently control the source evidence and no benchmark, aggregation, exclusivity or post-termination rights are secured. Customer-isolated records are reproducible, and incumbents can add the same fields and reports.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: An audit-led, focused product may be easier to adopt than a full PLM deployment and could outperform generic document storage. Evidence does not yet show a material advantage over specialist low-cost PPWR products or bundled incumbent platforms in outcomes, speed, trust, usability or total cost.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The regulation's general application from August 2026 and explicit documentation and supplier-information duties create a timely buying window. Momentum is moderated because major substantive measures phase in through 2030 and competitors have already launched overlapping products.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Consultants, laboratories and converters are logically aligned referral sources, and a paid audit is a practical entry offer compatible with focused B2B selling. No signed channel relationship, observed lead flow, conversion rate, sales cycle or validated CAC supports repeatable acquisition yet.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The software and document-AI components fit the founder and the 75,000 PLN experiment is feasible part-time with contractors. Execution still requires packaging-regulatory expertise, supplier participation, security and contractual permissions, while interpretation liability, onboarding labor, incumbent response and strict separation from employer resources are material risks.

highest_value_structural_change: Narrow the product around one packaging category and approval workflow where 2026 obligations are immediate, then secure a laboratory or converter channel plus standardized customer and supplier permissions that create reusable evidence benchmarks unavailable to customer-isolated tools.
main_structural_strength: A regulation-driven, recurring supplier-evidence workflow can be entered through paid readiness audits and converted into a scalable approval record that fits the founder's technical skills and capital constraints.
primary_score_limiter: The proposed control point is not yet controlled: competing tools already cover the workflow, while customer acquisition, premium pricing, unit economics and durable data rights are all unvalidated.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Direct substitutes advertise overlapping declaration, supplier-tool, repository and evidence-trail functionality from €29 per month or €999 annually, and Specright already bundles supplier collaboration, packaging specifications and automated PPWR declarations; this materially weakens differentiation, pricing power and domination potential.
